chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Sindiy ibn Muhammad from 'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Anfal (spoils of war) is from the Anfal (plurality/abundance), and in the Surah Al-Anfal, it refers to the cutting off of the nose.

key_terms.الْأَنْفَالُ: Plenties, abundances, or spoils of war
key_terms.سُورَةِ الْأَنْفَالِ: The Chapter of Spoils of War (Quran Chapter 8)

ai.seo_question: What is the linguistic meaning of 'Al-Anfal' in the Quran according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the linguistic duality of the term 'Anfal', linking the Quranic concept of 'spoils of war' to its root meaning of 'plenty' or 'abundance'. It further offers a unique exegetical perspective connecting the Surah's title to the physical act of 'jad' al-anf' (cutting the nose), reflecting pre-Islamic customs or specific scholarly interpretations of the root's semantic range. This entry serves as a key example of how early Shia scholars utilized etymological analysis to deepen the understanding of Quranic terminology within the context of fiqh and tafsir.
